# External build and runtime dependencies

The Phoenix implementation, selected CUDA sources, shader generators, tests and
packaging tools are in this repository. Install the components below separately;
their binaries are not generated by Phoenix. These are the versions inspected on
the verification machine on 2026-10-11, not claims that every older/newer version
works. Preserve each vendor's applicable distribution notices when packaging.

## Build tools

| Component | Tested version | Needed for / setup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python x64 | 3.14; scripts target 3.11+ | Build orchestration and offline tests; install from [Python](https://www.python.org/downloads/windows/) |
| MSVC x64 Build Tools | Visual Studio 2026 18.9.3, compiler toolset 14.51.36231 | All Windows C++ targets; install Desktop development with C++ and x64 tools from [Microsoft](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/) |
| Windows SDK | 10.0.26100.0 | Windows headers, D3D12, resource compiler and system import libraries; install through Visual Studio |
| NVIDIA NGX headers | Header API 1.5.0, `NVSDK_NGX_VERSION_API_MACRO=0x15` | Addon, native probe and D3D12 offload tests; obtain the SDK from [NVIDIA NGX](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/ngx); pass the directory containing `nvsdk_ngx.h` as `--ngx-sdk` |
| CUDA Toolkit | 13.1 | Native RTX and portable CUDA; obtain from the [CUDA archive](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-toolkit-archive); pass `bin/nvcc.exe`. Production native target is `sm_120` |
| ROCm SDK core | Package `rocm-sdk-core` 10.1.0; HIP header version 7.16.26385, git `7da43026e4` | Portable HIP; install a Windows SDK for the target GPU using [TheRock's package instructions](https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/RELEASES.md). Pass the SDK core directory containing `include/` and `lib/` via `--hip-sdk`; tested target `gfx1036`. Package and HIP component versions are different |
| Intel LLVM / DPC++ | Nightly 2026-10-07, DPC++ 7.2.0 prerelease, LLVM 24.0.0git, commit `95ed2199718412903ef28d5c9c1c51af2efe15b2` | Portable SYCL; extract the Windows compiler archive from [Intel LLVM releases](https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/doc/Releases.md), pass `bin/clang++.exe` via `--sycl-compiler` |
| Vulkan headers / glslang | Vulkan headers 1.4.365; glslang 16.6.0 | Portable Vulkan shader build; obtain SDK/tools from [LunarG](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/sdk/home). The builder expects `headers/include/vulkan/vulkan.h` and `glslang/bin/glslang.exe` under `--vulkan-deps`; arrange those two directories or use a junction to the installed include/tools folders |
| NumPy | 2.5.2 (requires Python 3.12+) | Optional offline synthetic fixture generation only: `python -m pip install numpy==2.5.2`. Neither the addon nor C++ runners require NumPy, Python or Torch at runtime |

The tested Vulkan setup combines independently supplied headers and glslang;
it is not identified as a single LunarG SDK release. NGX's number above is the
API macro in the supplied headers, not an inferred SDK download release.

## Runtime components

| Route | Components supplied externally | Inspected versions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All games | ReShade with addon support, Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime, Windows D3D12/DXGI | Match the MSVC x64 runtime to the compiler; [Microsoft runtime downloads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist) |
| Native RTX / CUDA | Compatible NVIDIA driver; CUDA driver API comes from the driver | RTX 5080, NVIDIA driver 616.64 used for local verification; `sm_120` is not portable to older GPU architectures |
| HIP | `amdhip64_7.dll`, `amd_comgr.dll`, `rocm_kpack.dll` from the same installed ROCm SDK | `amdhip64_7.dll` product 10.0.3684.0; COMGR 3.5.0.0. These DLL versions differ from the SDK package number |
| SYCL | `sycl9.dll`, `ur_loader.dll`, `ur_adapter_opencl.dll`, `ur_win_proxy_loader.dll`, OpenCL loader and a device ICD | SYCL 9.0; Unified Runtime loader/adapter 0.12.0; proxy loader 9.0.0-0; use the matching compiler distribution |
| SYCL CPU | Private Intel OpenCL CPU ICD and its complete runtime directory, including `.rtl`, `.o`, `.cfg`, SVML and TBB libraries | `intelocl64.dll` 2026.6.0.0.0617; TBB 2023.1.0; SVML 3.8.0. Obtain a compatible CPU runtime using [Intel's setup guide](https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/doc/GetStartedGuide.md). CPU ICD files are vendor components, not Phoenix build outputs |
| Vulkan | Vendor graphics driver with Vulkan loader and the required shader capabilities | NVIDIA RTX 5080 and AMD Radeon integrated graphics were the reference devices; build success does not certify other devices |
| NVIDIA DLSS Super Resolution (optional) | Compatible RTX rendering GPU/driver, game's initialized NGX context, and separately supplied `nvngx_dlss.dll` beside the game | `nvngx_dlss.dll` 310.3.0.0; local API/resolve checks passed on RTX 5080 at active 1280×720 and 640×360 to 1920×1080. Obtain the runtime/SDK from [NVIDIA DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS). Separate from `nvngx_dlssnr.dll` |
| Intel XeSS (optional) | `libxess.dll` and its required dependencies beside the game; compatible D3D12 rendering GPU/driver | SDK commit `de0fb9c1c510661c571164e1418ceca8101dab69`, `libxess.dll` 2.0.2.68; runtime API/resolve checks on RTX 5080; Intel hardware untested. Obtain from [Intel XeSS](https://github.com/intel/xess). Public headers are vendored; no import library needed |
| Model loading | A compatible, separately obtained `nvngx_dlssnr.dll`, or a user-supplied compatible model folder | Saved regression tests pin DLL SHA-256 `e16bcf15e16e13f527491cdf7845b2fe6521a738d8f7c9c721866a8496e1fc8e`; no model data is included |

Use `native_runtime/package_build.py --dependency PATH_TO_DLL` repeatedly for
vendor DLLs. Use `--opencl-cpu PATH_TO_PRIVATE_ICD_DIRECTORY` for the CPU ICD;
also build the `opencl_cpu_proxy` target. The package uses the repository's proxy
as `opencl_cpu/OpenCL.dll`, not a copied vendor loader in that private directory.
The private ICD is not registered globally. Install GPU drivers normally.

CPU-only packages need none of the optional GPU SDK/runtime distributions.
Omit unsupported routes rather than marking them validated. A release's
`validation_manifest.json` lists exactly the devices and resolutions tested.

## What Git intentionally excludes

`build/` contains generated code, PTX, cubins, shaders, binaries, packaging
resources and new test receipts. Their current build recipes are tracked.
Local models, vendor binaries, game configuration/backups, captures and old
measurements remain ignored. They are external or historical data, not missing
implementation source, and are not promised to be recreatable byte for byte.

## Offline temporal-upscaler validation

`tools/build_validation_tools.py NAME --ngx-sdk PATH` builds the XeSS probe
without additional link libraries. To initialize an isolated NVIDIA NGX context
for the offline DLSS SR probe, also pass `--ngx-library PATH_TO_nvsdk_ngx_d.lib`
from the official SDK (`lib/Windows_x86_64/x64/`, Release `/MD`). This extra
library is used only by the validation harness; the addon reuses the host
game's NGX context and does not initialize or shut it down.

Run `temporal_upscaler_probe.exe dlss|xess RUNTIME_DIRECTORY RESULT_JSON`
(optionally `--padded`) on an idle compatible GPU. It checks a synthetic
stationary scene and the addon resolve/upscale/fence path; it does not certify
gameplay temporal quality, Intel hardware performance or NVIDIA NR inference.
